parts.latex: By considering the equation of the tangent to $y=x^2-1$ at the point $(a,a^2-1)$, find the equations of the two tangents to $y=x^2-1$ which pass through $(3,-8)$.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{226_q31_1}
$$y = x^2 - 1$$
$$y' = 2x$$
Gradient of tangent at $x = a$ is $2a$.

$\therefore$ Equation of tangent at $(a, a^2 - 1)$ is
$$\begin{aligned} y - \left(a^2 - 1\right) &= 2a(x - a) \\ y - a^2 + 1 &= 2ax - 2a^2 \\ y &= 2ax - a^2 - 1 \end{aligned}$$
Since the tangent passes through $(3, -8)$, then
$$\begin{aligned} -8 &= 6a - a^2 - 1 \\ a^2 - 6a - 7 &= 0 \\ (a-7)(a+1) &= 0 \\ a &= 7 \text{ or } a = -1 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ The equations of the two tangents are:

When $a = 7$,
$$\begin{aligned} y &= 2(7)x - 7^2 - 1 \\ y &= 14x - 50 \end{aligned}$$
and when $a = -1$,
$$\begin{aligned} y &= 2(-1)x - (-1)^2 - 1 \\ y &= -2x - 2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitute $(3, -8)$ into the equation of the tangent at $x = a$, or equivalent merit
Finds the equation of the tangent at $x = a$, or equivalent merit
Finds the gradient of the tangent at $x = a$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Find the equation of the normal to the curve $y=\left(x+\dfrac{2}{x}\right)^2$ when $x=2$.

Equation of normal:
$$\begin{aligned}y-9&=-\dfrac{1}{3}(x-2)\\ -3y+27&=x-2\\ x+3y-29&=0\end{aligned}$$

The tangent and normal meet where

When $x=-2$, $y=-1$:
$$\begin{aligned} a(-2)^2+b(-2)+c &= -1\\ \dfrac{1}{2}\times 4+4\times(-2)+c &= -1\\ -6+c &= -1\\ \therefore\ c &= 5\end{aligned}$$

770.stem:
Consider the curve $y=ax^2+bx+c$, where $a\ne 0$.

At a particular point, the tangent and normal to the curve are given by

$t(x)=5(x+1)$ and $n(x)=-\dfrac{x}{5}-\dfrac{1}{5}$ respectively.

The curve has a maximum turning point at $x=\dfrac{1}{4}$

parts.latex: Show that the point of intersection of the tangent and the normal is $(-1,0)$
Find the values of $a$, $b$ and $c$.

solutions.latex:
The tangent and normal meet where $t(x)=n(x)$:
$$\begin{aligned} 5(x+1)&=-\dfrac{x}{5}-\dfrac{1}{5}\\ 5(5x+5)&=-x-1\\ 25x+25&=-x-1\\ 25x+x&=-1-25\\ 26x&=-26\\ x&=-1\end{aligned}$$
$$t(-1)=5(-1+1)=0$$
$\therefore$ the point of intersection of the tangent and the normal is $(-1,0)$.

$$\begin{aligned} y&=ax^2+bx+c\\ y'&=2ax+b\end{aligned}$$
The gradient of the tangent and the curve is the same at $(-1,0)$:
$$\begin{aligned} 2a(-1)+b&=5\\ -2a+b&=5 &&(1)\end{aligned}$$
The maximum turning point is at $x=\dfrac{1}{4}$, so $y'\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} 2a\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)+b&=0\\ \dfrac{a}{2}+b&=0 &&(2)\end{aligned}$$
Subtracting (1) from (2):
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{a}{2}+2a&=-5\\ \dfrac{5a}{2}&=-5\\ a&=-\dfrac{5\times2}{5}=-2\end{aligned}$$
From (2):
$$b=-\dfrac{a}{2}=1$$
For $c$, substitute the point $(-1,0)$, $a$ and $b$ into $y=ax^2+bx+c$:
$$\begin{aligned} 0&=-2(-1)^2+1(-1)+c\\ c-1-2&=0\\ c&=3\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ a=-2,\ b=1,\ c=3$$

$$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2-2$$
The gradient of the tangent at $(-1,1)$ is
$$m_1=3(-1)^2-2=1$$
The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so $m_2=-\dfrac{1}{m_1}=-1$.

Equation of the normal:
$$\begin{aligned} y-y_1 &= m_2(x-x_1) \\ y-1 &= -1(x+1) \\ y-1 &= -x-1 \\ y &= -x \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the gradient of the normal, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Find $f'(x)$.

$$\begin{aligned} u&=x & v&=x^2-1\\ u'&=1 & v'&=2x\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} f'(x) &= \dfrac{x^2 - 1 - 2x^2}{\left(x^2-1\right)^2} \\ &= \dfrac{-x^2 - 1}{\left(x^2-1\right)^2} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore f'(x) = \dfrac{-x^2 - 1}{\left(x^2-1\right)^2}$$
criteria: Uses the quotient rule, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: A normal to the graph of $y=2\sqrt{x}$ has the equation $y=-3x+b$. Find the value of $b$.

parts.latex: By considering the equation of the tangent to $y=x^2-1$ at the point $(a,a^2-1)$, find the equations of the two tangents to $y=x^2-1$ which pass through $(3,-8)$.

solutions.latex:
For $y=x^2-1$, $y'=2x$, so the gradient at $x=a$ is $2a$.

The tangent at $(a,a^2-1)$ is:

$$\begin{aligned} y-(a^2-1) &= 2a(x-a) \\ y-a^2+1 &= 2ax-2a^2 \\ y &= 2ax-a^2-1 \end{aligned}$$

If the tangent passes through $(3,-8)$:

$$\begin{aligned} 2a(3)-a^2-1 &= -8 \\ a^2-6a-7 &= 0 \\ (a-7)(a+1) &= 0 \end{aligned}$$

So $a=7$ or $a=-1$.

For $a=7$: $y=14x-50$.

For $a=-1$: $y=-2x-2$.

$$\therefore\ y=14x-50 \text{ and } y=-2x-2$$
criteria: Finds both values of $a$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Find, in general form, the equation of the normal to the curve $y = 2\sqrt{x}$ at the point on the curve where $x = 4$.

At $x=4$, the tangent gradient is $m_T=\dfrac{1}{2}$, so the normal gradient is $m_N=-2$.

The normal is
$$\begin{aligned} y-4&=-2(x-4)\\ y&=-2x+12\\ 2x+y-12&=0\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: Differentiate $\dfrac{x^3+2}{x-1}$.

parts.latex: Find $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\sqrt{x}\right)$.

Point $A(2e,1)$ lies on the function $h(x)$. The tangent to $h(x)$ at $A$ has equation $y=\dfrac{x}{2e}$.

parts.latex: Show that $B$ has coordinates $(e-2,3)$.

solutions.latex:
Write $g(x)=3h\left(2(x+2)\right)$. A point $(x,y)$ on $h$ maps to $\left(\dfrac{x}{2}-2,\,3y\right)$ on $g$.
$$B=\left(\dfrac{2e}{2}-2,\,3\times1\right)=(e-2,\,3)$$

Differentiate $g(x)=3h(2x+4)$ using the chain rule.
$$g'(x)=3h'(2x+4)\times2=6h'(2x+4)$$
At $B$, $x=e-2$, so $2x+4=2e$.
$$g'(e-2)=6h'(2e)$$
But $h'(2e)$ is the gradient of the tangent at $A$, which is $\dfrac{1}{2e}$.
$$g'(e-2)=6\times\dfrac{1}{2e}=\dfrac{3}{e}$$
The tangent at $B$ is
$$\begin{aligned} y-3 &= \dfrac{3}{e}\left(x-(e-2)\right) \\ ey-3e &= 3x-3e+6 \\ 3x-ey+6 &= 0 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Gradient at $B$ equals $\dfrac{3}{e}$, or equivalent merit

4136.stem: The line $y=24(x-1)$ is tangent to the curve $y=ax^3+bx^2+4$ at $x=2$.

parts.latex: Using the fact that the tangent meets the curve to show that $2a+b=5$.
By finding another relationship between $a$ and $b$, find the values of $a$ and $b$.

solutions.latex:
When $x=2$ the tangent has
$$\begin{aligned}y&=24(2-1)\\&=24\end{aligned}$$
The point of contact is $(2,24)$, which also lies on the curve $y=ax^3+bx^2+4$.
$$\begin{aligned}24&=a\times 2^3+b\times 2^2+4\\24&=8a+4b+4\\20&=8a+4b\\5&=2a+b\quad\ldots(1)\end{aligned}$$

The gradient of the curve at $x=2$ equals the gradient of the tangent, $24$.
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=3ax^2+2bx\\24&=3a\times 2^2+2b\times 2\\24&=12a+4b\\6&=3a+b\quad\ldots(2)\end{aligned}$$
Subtracting (1) from (2):
$$a=1$$
Substituting into (1): $2+b=5$.
$$\therefore\ a=1,\ b=3$$

parts.latex:
At a point $P(k-2,y)$ on $f(x)=kx^2-kx-k^2$ the gradient of the tangent is $3k-8$.

solutions.latex:
The gradient of the tangent is $f'(x)$.
$$f'(x)=2kx-k$$
At $x=k-2$:
$$\begin{aligned}f'(k-2)&=2k(k-2)-k\\&=2k^2-5k\end{aligned}$$
Equate this to the given gradient $3k-8$.
$$\begin{aligned}2k^2-5k&=3k-8\\2k^2-8k+8&=0\\k^2-4k+4&=0\\(k-2)^2&=0\end{aligned}$$
$$k=2$$
This is option A.

parts.latex: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = \dfrac{1}{4x+1}$ at the point $(0, 1)$.

solutions.latex:
Write $y = (4x+1)^{-1}$ and differentiate using the chain rule:
$$y' = -4(4x+1)^{-2} = \dfrac{-4}{(4x+1)^2}$$
When $x=0$:
$$y' = \dfrac{-4}{(4\times0+1)^2} = -4$$
The tangent at $(0,1)$ is
$$\begin{aligned} y-1 &= -4(x-0) \\ y &= -4x+1 \end{aligned}$$
